statement: For generic zero-sum frequencies and positive rank-one coupling parameters in the polynomial Kuramoto formulation (4), the complex root count after identifying configurations differing by a common phase shift is 2^n−2. This counts complex algebraic solutions, not only physical phases.

answer.text: The generic complex root count is 2^n−2.

notes:
Count is for the polynomial formulation (4) modulo shift; the real-equilibrium algorithm uses conditions IC1–IC3.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_a3847adad435e1cb; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.
scope: n oscillators, symmetric rank-one couplings k_i k_j with positive k_i; zero-sum frequencies; quotient by common phase shift. The equations use coupling coefficient k_i k_j/n: ω_i=(1/n)Σ_j k_i k_j sin(θ_i−θ_j).
